A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoEval research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original LLM truth-maintenance and verification experiments, o1 evaluation, few-shot comparisons, and repeated-run analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices report expanded LLM/LRM experiments, locally measured HumanEval results, and original verifier-error and dataset-diversity analyses.

M1.justification: The CFG sampling algorithm, vocabulary generation, same-model formal-to-natural-to-formal translation with context clearing, and formal equivalence verification remain unchanged. The parameterized/calibrated score terminology organizes calculations already present in v1, including Appendix K.4.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same five generated datasets and FOLIO, LogiEval, HumanEval, and BBH tasks. Renaming 3-SAT to 3-CNF preserves the generated task. Additional models, larger samples, and diagnostics do not introduce new domains, languages, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Beyond v1's six core LLMs and o1, v2 evaluates numerous additional models, including Gemma-2, Granite-3.0, Qwen-2.5, Yi, and additional Llama/Phi variants (Table 7; Figures 18–20). Separate evaluations add Claude 3.0 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1 (Appendix N.1; Figure 6).

E3.justification: The evaluation expands to model configurations spanning approximately 1B–70B parameters and replaces literature-only HumanEval comparisons with local measurements. LRM sampling increases from five to ten examples per operator category, approximately 200 to 400 examples. New diagnostics also introduce classwise precision/recall and verifier breakdowns restricted to complexity at most 20.

E4.justification: New Appendix L analyzes verifier false positives and noncompliance and supplies two explicit failure cases. Appendix M examines structural diversity after vocabulary normalization, while Tables 15–20 add classwise benchmark error analyses. The existing few-shot comparison and earlier translation-error examples are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 newly reports five-run averages for locally measured HumanEval results. Appendix H retains the same ten-run standard-deviation analysis. The revised LRM section omits v1's explicit three-run averaging statement; this omission does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive model and diagnostic results and revises cross-benchmark summaries. FOLIO(R; NL) correlation changes from 0.95 to 0.81 (v1 Figure 3; v2 Figure 4). Table 6 adds locally measured GPT-4o HumanEval accuracy of 91.8 alongside the previously cited 90.2. Changed cohorts and measurement sources preclude interpreting these as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Definitions 2.1–2.2 remove inverse-equivalence requirements from the translation definitions, and Definition 2.3 changes from a property of a given sequence to a universally quantified LLM property. The human/coffee formalization is corrected. The existing false-positive derivation and Appendix B coverage argument remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: dynamic annotation-free evaluation, formal verification, scalability, prediction of other benchmark performance, and weak truth maintenance by current LLMs/LRMs. Expanded experiments support these retained claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 attributes weaker LogiEval(FOL) correlation to class imbalance and answer bias, replacing v1's emphasis on GPT-4o-mini's difficulty with longer reasoning chains. It adds positive-verifier-bias interpretation, uses a reported 0.66% timeout rate to qualify the verifier limitation, and removes the explicit English-only limitation.

D1.justification: v2 adds explicit code-access information, exact model identifiers in Table 7, hardware information for larger models, and clearer dataset complexity limits. These extend an already detailed appendix; the existing algorithm, prompts, package versions, and generation hyperparameters largely remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds LLM-as-judge and self-refinement positioning with Zheng, Shankar, Xu, and Madaan citations, alongside references supporting newly evaluated models. Guan and LeanDojo references are removed. The central positioning against static, human-annotated benchmarks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is substantially reorganized: metrics and false-positive analysis move into Section 3.2, dataset generation becomes Section 3.3, and model assessment precedes benchmark-predictiveness analysis. The introduction, formal framework, and conclusion are extensively revised, with terminology changes and additional appendix sections.

P2.justification: Core plots are reordered, additional model curves appear in grey, and predictive-power bars are sorted and grouped by metric type. Figure 6 is redesigned for two LRMs. Figures 18–23 and Tables 7–20 add expanded per-model displays and diagnostics; Table 6 separates computed and published scores.

improvement.justification: v1's surrogate-benchmark claim relied on six core LLMs and externally sourced HumanEval scores. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through a broader model range, local five-run HumanEval measurements, and detailed verifier and benchmark-error diagnostics. Corrected definitions and additional reproducibility information also help. Inconsistent model counts and some dataset labels remain, but the overall gains in empirical support and auditability are substantial.
